x: Teddy Read, the sprinter, sent to Canada, and a letter is eagerly awaited.
He has recently become engaged to the sister of Teddy Read, our well known sprinter. Teddy, until rececntly, was with the R.A.F. in Canada, but has now returned home with his " Wings."
Teddy Read is now, we understand, in Tunisia, and has brought down his first "Jerry." Good shooting, Teddy! We have also heard he was in the W.A.F. also M.E.F.
Teddy Read, we understand from Lilian, is in the Bengal jungle, amongst snakes and alligators, looking for Japs—apparently enjoying himself.
Teddy Read is still in India, and, according to Lilian, has just gained his first ring and become a Pilot Officer.
Teddy Read is now a Fying Officer attached to the 14th Army; he is grounded for a time but is quite happy. This we learn from Lilian, who also informs us that
Among the sprinters, Teddy Read improved by leaps and bounds as the season progressed, and was given good support by Dicky Dumbrill and Jack Frost.

Jack Frost ran second in the 100 Yards, and also finished third in the 220, which was won by Teddy Read. Syd Jarlett and Bob Wise finished second and third in the 440, and Len Marchant won the 880 Yards, with Alf Orton fourth.
Teddy Read made no mistake and went right away to win in quite good time with Stan Botwright, the past holder, second and Dicky Dumbrill third.

In the 4 x 100 Yards Relay our four ran second to Achilles, our runners were Teddy Read, Dicky Dumbrill, Jack Frost and Michael Broadbent. Another Relay success was at Guildford, Lulham, Hawkins, Osmint and Read each pulled away from their rivals.
